questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

Is the older person always more wiser than the younger one?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'more wiser'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence is asking whether it is necessary that an older person is always more wise than a younger person. 

__
 
• The part of the sentence that we are looking at here is** 'comparative adjectives'.**
 
• This is because the **sentence is comparing the wisdom of an older person to that of a younger person,** and since** 'wise' is an adjective**. It becomes a comparative adjective. 
 
• When using the comparative term 'wiser', there is no need for the determine 'more' as that is already implied by the use of the comparative term. 

Correct Sentence- Is the older person always wiser than the younger one?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are basically 2 types of adjectives when it comes to intensity. 
 
• 
 
 
 

 
 
**Adjectives**

 
 
 
**Formation**

 
 
 
**Examples**

 
 
 

 
 
Comparative

 
 
 
This compares only 2 nouns with each other

 
 
 
Wiser, Angrier, Calmer, etc. 

 
 
 

 
 
Superlative

 
 
 
This implies that the current noun is superior to all unit of that category. 

 
 
 
Wisest, Angriest, Calmest, etc.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

__Would you mind help__ me with these questions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **would you mind helping **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about the narrator asking someone if they would help the narrator with some questions. 

 
• The sentence is in the **present continuous tense.** This means that the **action in the sentence is currently happening and is ongoing, it isn't over yet. **
 
• This means that the **verb in the sentence should be in its 'ing' form. **
 
• This rules out** option no. 4 as the verb isn't in its 'ing' form. **
 
• Option 2 is incorrect as the **preposition 'for' implies a purpose**, in this case, it would be used after the person - if they choose to - helps the narrator. 
 
 
• *"Thank you **for helping** me."*
 
 
 
• Option 3 is incorrect as **there is a need for improvement** in the sentence since the original verb in the sentence isn't in the present continuous tense. 

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

questions.question:
**Select the option that means the same as the given idiom.**

Hit the nail on the head
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **accurately right**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hit the nail on the head: **This means to identify something exactly; to come to the accurate and correct conclusion. Derives from the fact that a nail that is hit perfectly on the head with a hammer would go in correctly.
 
• **Accurately right: **To be perfectly correct and right about something. 
 
• *E.g. Aditi was accurately right about the questions that would appear in the examination. *
 
• Thus, it is clear that** 'hit the nail on the head' and 'accurately right' are similar phrases. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Option 2 is a **literal rendition** of the idiom given in the question and thus cannot be the meaning.
 
• Option 3 is a **loose** **version of another idiom - 'fight tooth and nail**' - which means to fight with all of one's might. 
 
• Option 4 is again in the** literal sense of the idiom and is also very generic**, it does not mention 'nails' or a hammer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• **Knowing what an idiom means **(a common saying or phrase that does not necessarily literally mean what the words refer to) would be **very helpful in understanding which of the options is synonymous with the question. **

Thus, the correct answer is **option 1. **

questions.question: **Directions: Select the most appropriate option that will fill in the blank number 3.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** through. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how with the help of the festival Tilak was able to gather support for the national movement. 

 
• The preposition **'through' implies the act of getting to something using something else as the medium**
 
• In this case, **Tilak reached the stage of gathering support by using the means or medium of the celebration of the festival. **
 
• **Option 1** is incorrect as the **festival is not a tangible thing which can have something 'within' - inside - it. **
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect as the **whole passage focuses on Tilak emphasising on increasing the importance of the festival**, then **why would he achieve his goal 'without' - in the absence of - of the festival's celebration. **
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect as there is **no mention of Tilak physically gathering support while the celebration was actually going on. **
 
• 'Throughout' would mean from the beginning to the end of something, and Tilak doing this is not specified in the passage.

**Thus, the correct answer is option 2. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

A team of doctors __is focusing over treatment of cancer__ at an early age.

options.text: is focusing on to treatment of cancer
is focusing on the treatment of cancer
is focusing in treatment of cancer

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **focusing on the treatment of cancer **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how a team of doctors are is paying attention and working on the treatment of cancer in its early stages.

 
• The** part of speech that needs to the replaced in the underlined section of the sentence is a preposition** - over. 
 
• The preposition '**over' refers to the act of being higher up than the item in question and then looking down from there. **
 
 
• *​Hence, there is need for improvement. *
 
 
 
• When it comes to **'focus' it is an abstract concept **and hence **cannot have a particular direction like** - above, below, over or under. 
 
• To **'focus on' something means to pay all one's attention to it,** to direct all of one's energy towards it. 
 
• '**Focus' does not have a physical or tangible existence **and thus **nothing can be 'in' focus nor can focus be placed 'in' something. **

Thus, the correct answer is** option 2. **

• Of the **base form of the verb 'is'**, the **singular form in the simple present tense is 'has' and the plural form for the same is 'have'. **
 
• Thus, the **'have been working', needs to be replaced with 'has been working'. **

Thus, the correct answer is **option 4. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

Our society is _______ by the evil of corruption; the integrity of even senior officials is disputed.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 2 i.e. endangered. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how our society is put in danger and peril by the existence of corruption. 

__
 
• Let's look at the meaning of the words given as options:
 
 
• **Indicated:** Past tense of 'indicate', which means to point out to something or to show something. 
 
• **Endangered**: Past tense of 'endanger', which means to put someone/something in harm's way. 
 
• **Specified**: Past tense of 'specify', which means to identify and state something clearly. 
 
• **Identified**: Past tense of 'identify', which means to recognize someone or distinguish them from others. 
 
 
 
• The state of corruption is **not the only concept to exist in our society**, there are various aspects of society. 
 
• Thus options that **imply that 'corruption' is the only aspect of society will be eliminated**. Option 4 is incorrect. 
 
• The latter phrase implies that the** verb in the blank has a negative connotation. **
 
• Thus, options like **'indicated' and 'specified' which are neutral verbs will be eliminated. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• The reader should try and **understand the tone of the sentence** in order to understand what the connotation of the answer may be.
 
• This would help them identify or eliminate certain options. 

**Thus, the correct answer is option 2. **

Let's look at the meaning of all the words given in the options

The sentence talks about how Lokmanya Tilak campaigned to celebrate the festival on a grand scale, throughout Maharashtra.

• The word in the blank has to used for a **'countable noun', a noun that can be quantified. **
 
• Thus the blank has to **have an article i.e. a, an or the. **
 
• Option 1 cannot be used since the **word following the blank doesn't start with a vowel or vowel sound. **
 
• Option 2 is **incorrect as it is not an article.**
 
• Option 4 is also **incorrect as it not an article. **

**Article**

 
 
 
**Usage**

 
 
 
**Example**

 
 
 

 
 
A

 
 
 
Used for common nouns which begin with a consonant or a consonant’s phonetic sound.

 
 
 
A person who cannot keep their word to themselves is not worth trusting.

 
 
 

 
 
An

 
 
 
Used for common nouns which begin with a vowel or a vowel’s phonetic sound.

 
 
 
An apple which fell from a tree and hit Newton on the head changed the course of physics.

 
 
 

 
 
The

 
 
 
Used for proper nouns, which are countable and unique.

 
 
 
The ‘Taj Mahal’ is a sight to behold from near and afar.

 
 
 

 

 Thus, the correct answer is **option 3. **

questions.question:
**From the given options, identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.**

When I asked for directions, he gave me many wrong informations.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **wrong informations. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how the narrator asked a person for directions, and the person gave him a lot of wrong information. 

__
 
• The word **'information' is an abstract noun. **
 
• An abstract noun is **one that cannot be seen or heard or smelled**. It is just felt. 
 
• Since it is not **tangible it cannot be quanitified. **
 
• Because it cannot be quantified, it can **neither be singular or plural. **
 
• Thus, as per the rules of grammar **'information' cannot be plural.

 **

**​Correct Sentence- **When I asked for directions, he gave me many** **wrong** information.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• Not only is it important to **identify a word as a noun or a verb or any other part of speech** but it may also be immensely helpful to understand and **identify what category they belong to within a part of speech. **
 
• This would help the reader come to the correct conclusion about why an option is incorrect. 

Thus, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: **Directions: Select the most appropriate option that will fill in the blank number 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how Lokmanya Tilak was able to gather support for a nationalist movement by encouraging the celebration of the 'Ganapati festival' as a national festival.

• **Option 3** is incorrect as **'nationalism' is not an event or feeling that occurs at a fixed time or for a fixed duration** and thus it cannot have a 'season'.

**Thus, the correct answer is option 1. **

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank.**

Many tourists in India visit the beautiful valley of Kashmir ______ in spring and summer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3 i.e. especially

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how a lot of tourists in India visit the valley of Kashmir, more often in the Spring and the Summer. 

__
 
• Given that the sentence is trying to **imply a specific period during which tourists prefer to visit the Valley of Kashmir**, we need an adverb that also implies this. 
 
• The use of the **determiner 'many' means that 'rarely' is an unlikely option** for the answer. 
 
• 'Frequently' implies that the **'many tourists' visit the Valley of Kashmir more than once**, whereas it is very unlikely that tourists visit the same place more than once during the same trip. Thus, this option is incorrect. 
 
• The sentence is **looking for an adverb - a word that modifies the meaning of a verb or an adjective or a word group - and 'general' is not an adverb, it is an adjective.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• Understanding what **part of grammar fits into the given blank **will help the reader understand what can be kept or eliminated. 

Thus, the correct answer is **option 3. **

questions.question:

One should be careful to check the grease and oil in _______ car occasionally for its smooth functioning
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'one's'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

The sentence talks about how 'one' should be careful when it comes to checking the grease and oil in one's car in order to make sure the car functions smoothly. 

__
 
• The pronoun **'one' is already mentioned**, and unless it is not possible to use the same pronoun **it should be used in the sentence in order to avoid confusion. **
 
• The blank also** implies possession, the 'car' that belongs to 'one'. **
 
• Thus the contraction **'one's' needs to be used - instead of 'one' - in order to imply possession. **
 
• 'Ones' refers to more than 1 'one', it is a plural noun, while **we are looking at a singular pronoun. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• The reader should pay **specific attention to the apostrophes and the type of pronoun** that is being used elsewhere in the sentence. 
 
• This would help them understand **what type of pronoun should be used in the blank.** 

**Thus, the correct answer is option 4.**

questions.question:

One who makes an eloquent public speech

• **Debater:** A person who argues about a subject, especially in a formal manner. 
 
• **Speaker: **A person who delivers a speech or a lecture
 
• **Orator: **A skilled and fluent public speaker.

questions.question:

The sentence talks about how the subject of the sentence ('he') is as good as Suresh if in case he isn't better.

• *E.g. The people in the audience are getting bored.* 
 
 
 
• For the verb form, **'is' is the singular form.**
 
 
• *E.g. Rosa is really good at riding a motorcycle. *
 
 
 
• Thus, the** 'are' needs to be replaced with 'is'. **

Thus, the correct answer is **option 1. **

• As can be seen from the **apostrophes before and after 'Discovery of India'**, it can be deduced that it is the **title or name of something. **
 
• The use of the **preposition 'by' before 'Jawaharlal Nehru' implies that he is the agent carrying out the action in the sentence.**
 
• Since there is only one title, it can be assumed that the** item is singular. **
 
• This means that the **verb in the blank should also be singular. **
 
• Thus, **options 1 and 4 **are eliminated because they have a **plural verb 'have'**. 
 
• Option 2 is incorrect because the **absence of the verb 'been' implies that 'Jawaharlal Nehru' is something that has been written by 'Discovery of India', and this not true. ( we need the passive form)**
